questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a point has several polar descriptions
questions.stem: Why can two different polar entries name the same point in the tank?

answer.exemplar: A polar entry fixes a direction and a signed distance, and both of those can be changed without moving the point. Adding a full turn to the angle leaves the ray the same, and replacing a negative radius by its magnitude while adding half a turn also leaves the same point, because the ray is reversed exactly as much as the sign is dropped. The coordinates of a point are therefore not unique in polar form, unlike in Cartesian form.

questions.explanation: Adding a full turn to the angle changes nothing, and reversing the ray while keeping the distance also names the same point. Cartesian coordinates are unique, but polar entries are not, which is why a conversion must be handled carefully.
questions.hint: Angles can be shifted by full turns without moving the point.
